common.integrityBody: Something in the BridgeBox folder no longer matches the original. If you didn't edit these files yourself, the copy you're running may have been tampered with — reinstall from a source you trust.

home.betaTooltipBody: BridgeBox looks simple on the surface, but there's a lot happening underneath, and it still needs real-world testing before it's rock-solid. Once it's proven stable, this badge goes away.
home.howToConnectButton: How do I connect the game?
home.steamIntro: Here's how to point your Steam copy of Jackbox at BridgeBox. Follow along and you'll be set in a minute.
home.steamStep1: Open Steam and go to your LIBRARY.
home.steamStep2: Right-click the game you want to connect and open Properties.
home.steamStep3: In the window that opens, go to General and set the launch options to this:
home.steamStep5: That's it — your game is now wired up to BridgeBox. Go ahead and launch it!
home.otherIntro: Here's how to point your local copy of Jackbox at BridgeBox. Follow along and you'll be set in a minute.
home.otherLead: There are a couple of ways to do this — pick whichever fits.
home.otherWay1Step1: Create a shortcut to your game's .exe and put it somewhere handy.
home.otherWay1Step2: Right-click the shortcut and open Properties.
home.otherWay1Step3: In the Target field, click right after the closing quote, add a space, and paste this:
home.otherWay1Step4: Click Apply, then close the window.
home.otherWay1Step5: Done — launch the game through this shortcut from now on and BridgeBox will do its job.
home.otherWay2Intro: This one means digging into the game's own files, but it lets you choose exactly which install talks to BridgeBox — useful if you have more than one.

settings.title: Settings
settings.languageHint: Takes effect right away, no restart needed
settings.autostartHint: Adds an admin-level Task Scheduler entry — the bypass can't run without it
settings.autostartMinimizedHint: No window at sign-in — BridgeBox waits quietly in the notification area
settings.startBridgeOnLaunchHint: The bridge comes up as soon as the app opens, no need to flip the switch
settings.minimizeToTrayHint: The X hides the window instead of killing the bypass mid-game. Quit from the tray icon's menu
settings.hideConsoleHint: The bypass runs in the background, no separate black window next to the app
settings.tempDirHint: Zapret updates get downloaded and unpacked here. Leave blank for the system Temp folder
settings.updateSectionDescription: Flowseal's DPI bypass engine — winws, WinDivert, and the payload files
settings.updateCheckOnStartupHint: BridgeBox checks for a new version on its own when it starts
settings.updateCheckHint: Checks the official repository for a newer release
settings.updateConfirmBody: The bridge will stop and every connection will close first — otherwise the files being replaced would still be in use. winws.exe, WinDivert, and the payload files all get swapped in. Strategies update too, but if you've edited one yourself, your version stays untouched — the new one is saved alongside it under a different name. If a game is in progress, it's worth finishing it first.
settings.updateStrategiesForked: {original} has your own changes, so it was left alone — the new version is saved as {fork}
settings.updateRestartBody: The new files only take effect after a restart. The bridge will stop.
settings.factoryResetHint: Puts the whole app back to its factory defaults
settings.factoryResetConfirmBody: The port, the zapret strategy, every setting — all back to defaults. The app restarts and walks you through first-time setup again. Your DPI bypass domain list is not affected.
settings.networkSectionDescription: Zapret and the DPI bypass strategy
settings.strategyHint: Flowseal's presets, grouped the same way they are in zapret/strategies/
settings.strategyTestHint: Pings the servers each strategy needs to reach
settings.strategyTargetSetHint: Which Jackbox servers each strategy gets checked against
settings.testHeavyHint: Runs every single strategy, including the slow ones under "Other" (Fake TLS Auto*, Simple Fake*) — takes longer
settings.hostlistHint: zapret uses this list to decide which traffic gets routed around DPI
settings.hostlistModalDescription: One hostname per line. Lines starting with "#" are comments.
settings.hostlistRestartNote: Takes effect the next time the bridge starts
settings.portHint: 127.0.0.1:PORT — all of your game's traffic goes here
settings.profilesSectionDescription: A profile is a server address plus the settings for its protocol. Ecast (Party Pack 7 and up) and Blobcast (Party Pack 1–6) run at the same time, each with its own active profile — there's no protocol to pick between.
settings.profilesPickerHint: Choose which profile to edit. Use the button below to make it the active one
settings.profilesKindHint: Decides which requests reach this address and which settings apply
settings.profilesRestartNote: Takes effect the next time the bridge starts
settings.profilesTransferHint: Take your profiles to another machine — as a file or as text
settings.profilesTransferModalDescription: Built-in profiles aren't included. Importing only adds — it won't overwrite what you already have or change which profile is active.
settings.profilesBuiltinNote: Built-in profile — its name, type, and address are locked, and it can't be deleted, so the protocol always has a server. The settings below are still yours to edit.
settings.profilesDeleteConfirmBody: It disappears from the list. If it was the active one, the protocol falls back to the official server.
settings.profilesEcastSettingsHint: Only affects this profile. Direct connections already work without this — turn it on if something isn't coming up
settings.profilesEcastForwardAllHint: Every path that isn't Blobcast's goes to this profile's address. Turn it off and only the paths listed below get through — everything else gets an error
settings.profilesEcastPathsHint: Comma-separated, each starting with "/". Only used when "proxy all traffic" is off. Doesn't affect Blobcast — it has its own path list
settings.profilesInterceptHint: Turn this off and the session goes straight to Jackbox, bypassing the bridge. Rooms still get created, but the game may fail to start or misbehave.
settings.profilesLocalNameHint: Hostname only — no "https://" and no port. The game appends the port itself, and anything else turns this into an address that doesn't exist.
settings.profilesLogFramesHint: Otherwise frames only show up at debug level, and that can flood the log
settings.profilesBlobcastPathsHint: Comma-separated. Which requests go to this address instead of Ecast
settings.profilesSocketioPortHint: The port the game opens its session on. Only change this for an unofficial server — it has to match the port in zapret's strategy filters, or DPI bypass won't work on it.
settings.resetPortConfirmBody: Goes back to the default (8443). Takes effect the next time the bridge starts.
settings.serverKeysHint: Comma-separated JSON fields holding the relay address. Turn off and the response passes through unchanged
settings.upstreamOriginHint: The header Jackbox's load balancer expects. Turn off and the game's own header is sent instead
settings.userAgentHint: Only used when the game doesn't send its own. Without a browser-looking UA, the API answers with 403
settings.strategyModalProgressNoTotal: Switching to each strategy and checking it…
settings.dirtyBridge: Settings changed. Restart the bridge for them to take effect.
settings.dirtyApp: Settings changed. Restart the app for them to take effect.

setup.welcomeBody: Let's set up a local bridge for a stable connection to Jackbox's servers — it only takes a minute.
setup.welcomeAnimationsHint: Turn off if your computer is on the slower side
setup.certBody: For the game to talk to the bridge securely, it needs a local certificate installed. It only works on this computer (localhost) and is completely safe.
setup.certWarning: Windows may ask you to confirm this in a system prompt.
setup.certRequiredBody: Without the local certificate, the game refuses the HTTPS connection and the bridge can't work. This step isn't optional.
setup.strategyBody: Every provider blocks things differently (DPI). We need to find a strategy that works on your connection.
setup.strategyHint: We'll try every strategy against Jackbox's Ecast and Blobcast servers and pick the fastest one. Takes a few minutes.
setup.strategyManualHint: Skips the test — for when you already know what works, or just want to get through setup faster.
setup.strategyProgressNoTotal: Switching to each strategy and checking it…
setup.strategyPickHint: Keep this one or pick a different one from the list.
setup.strategyNoneWorked: None of the strategies got a response. We'll continue with the default one — you can rerun this test later from Settings.
setup.strategySkipWarning: Skipping the test leaves the default strategy in place — the connection may be unstable.
setup.updatesBody: Zapret, the engine behind the bypass, gets updated regularly. Want BridgeBox to check for new versions automatically on startup?
setup.updatesAutoHint: Runs in the background and never holds up the app opening
setup.updatesManualHint: GitHub isn't always reachable from the kind of network this app exists for. You can run the check any time from Settings
setup.connectTitle: How do I connect the game?
setup.connectBody: The bridge is ready. To route your game through it, add this to the launch options (Steam) or the shortcut's Target field:
setup.connectNoScheme: No "https://" — the game won't accept an address with a scheme, it adds that itself.
setup.connectFootnote: The full guide — with animations, for Steam and for other copies — is always one click away from the home screen's "How do I connect the game?" button.
setup.doneBody: BridgeBox is configured and ready to go. Have fun!
